# CKW Elements - AI Agent Guide

CKW Elements is a token-first React design system. Build UI by importing tokens and components from the packages instead of copying styles from Storybook.

## Install

```bash
npm install @ckwag/tokens @ckwag/components
```

## Required App Setup

Import token CSS once in the app entry point:

```css
@import '@ckwag/tokens/tokens.css';
```

React applications can import components from either package root or the explicit React subpath:

```tsx
import React from 'react';
import { Button, InlineMessage, InputField, SegmentedControl } from '@ckwag/components';
```

```tsx
import React from 'react';
import { Button, InlineMessage, InputField, SegmentedControl } from '@ckwag/components/react';
```

If a bundler does not process CSS side-effect imports from packages, import the aggregate component CSS explicitly:

```css
@import '@ckwag/components/styles.css';
```

## Token Assets

These files are published with the deployed documentation for agents and build tooling:

- `tokens/tokens.css`: CSS custom properties and typography utility classes.
- `tokens/tokens.js`: JavaScript named exports and a default token map.
- `tokens/tokens.d.ts`: TypeScript declarations for JavaScript token exports.
- `tokens/tokens.json`: DTCG token source.

The npm token package also exports:

```ts
import tokens, { interactivePrimary, spacingM } from '@ckwag/tokens';
import '@ckwag/tokens/tokens.css';
import rawTokens from '@ckwag/tokens/tokens.json';
```

## Styling Rules

- Use only semantic tokens for component colors: `--text-primary`, `--background-default`, `--interactive-primary`, `--border-soft`.
- Do not use primitive color tokens in product components: avoid `--color-green-600`, `--color-grey-800`, and similar primitives.
- Never hardcode hex colors in repository UI code except Storybook theme configuration where Storybook requires raw colors.
- Use CKW green for primary actions. Do not substitute blue as the primary brand color.
- Use `font-family: var(--font-family-brand), sans-serif`.
- Prefer token spacing, radii, shadows, border weights, and typography variables over raw CSS values.

## Component APIs

### Button

```tsx
<Button type="Primary" size="Large">Save</Button>
```

- `type`: `Primary`, `Secondary`, `Tertiary`
- `size`: `Large`, `Medium`, `Small`
- `disabled`: boolean
- `fullWidth`: boolean
- `leadingIcon`: React node
- `trailingIcon`: React node
- `htmlType`: `button`, `submit`, `reset`

### InputField

```tsx
<InputField label="Name" placeholder="Enter name" errorText={error} />
```

- `label`: string
- `placeholder`: string
- `value`: string
- `onChange`: React input change handler
- `disabled`: boolean
- `optional`: boolean
- `errorText`: string
- `icon`: React node
- `showInfo`: boolean

### InlineMessage

```tsx
<InlineMessage status="Info" title="Statusmeldung">
  Hier steht eine kurze Erklaerung zum aktuellen Status oder zur naechsten Aktion.
</InlineMessage>
```

- `status`: `Info`, `Success`, `Error`
- `title`: React node
- `children`: React node
- `icon`: React node
- `showIcon`: boolean
- `breakpoint`: `Auto`, `Desktop`, `Mobile`

### SegmentedControl

```tsx
<SegmentedControl
  segments={[
    { value: 'list', label: 'List' },
    { value: 'grid', label: 'Grid' },
  ]}
  activeValue="list"
  onChange={setView}
/>
```

- `segments`: array of `{ value, label, icon }`
- `activeValue`: string
- `onChange`: `(value: string) => void`
- `type`: `Default`, `Fill`
- `contentMode`: `label`, `icon-label`, `icon-compact`

## Agent Skills

Use these deployed prompt files when an AI agent needs CKW-specific behavior:

- `skills/ckw-prototyping.md`: use for rapid UI prototyping.
- `skills/ckw-components.md`: use for reusable React components.

## Storybook Fetch Notes

Storybook builds to static files. It is not server-side rendered HTML per route. Agents should fetch these plain-text/static assets first:

- `llms.txt`
- `llms-full.txt`
- `tokens/tokens.css`
- `tokens/tokens.json`
- `skills/ckw-prototyping.md`
- `skills/ckw-components.md`

For story metadata, fetch Storybook's generated index from the deployed build:

- `index.json`
- `stories.json` if available in the deployed Storybook version

Use Storybook URLs for visual inspection and the static assets above for code generation context.
